brief:
BRIEF FOR TEAM TS3012, before meeting d. Based on meetings a to c only.

WHAT HAS BEEN DECIDED (CURRENT)
- The production cost target is set at approximately 12.5 Euros. [TS3012a: "The production price, twelve and a half Euros, approximately."]
- Market research indicates 75% of users find remotes ugly, 50% use few buttons, and teletext has a relevance of 6.5/10. [TS3012b: "seventy five percent of the users find most remote controls ugly"; TS3012b: "uh fifty percent say they only So that's the most important things"]
- The remote will be universal to serve the company's diverse customer base, and speech recognition will not be implemented yet. [TS3012b: "I think it's universal. I think we should go for universal"; TS3012b: "I don't think it should be implemented in a remote control yet"]
- The design will feature a leaner shape with a rounded top, round buttons (including the center), and a curved case. [TS3012c: "I think so because it looks leaner and we should just go with that"; TS3012c: "We'll just take the take the round button, suppose"]
- The remote will use push-buttons, an advanced chip (required for the LCD), regular batteries located in the largest part of the device, and a rubber case. [TS3012c: "Okay. So push-buttons we will use"; TS3012c: "Uh that's no longer an option, it has to be an advanced one now"]
- The team is focusing on the deluxe edition for younger customers, with volume and channel controls centered, and one top button designated for the favorite channel. [TS3012c: "I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want"; TS3012c: "We're definitely focussing on the younger people, 'cause that was our main goal"]
- The scroll wheel was voted out, and removable covers are excluded from the basic design. [TS3012c: "No r no scroll-wheel. Okay. Um I don't see anything missing really"; TS3012c: "that's not something we're working with in the basic design"]

WHAT CHANGED ALONG THE WAY
- The remote locator feature evolved from a general durability improvement to a beep, and finally to a combined beep and flash system. [TS3012b: "we need to get something on the on the remote to find it somewhere"; TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote"]
- The case material decision shifted from ruling out wood to confirming rubber as the final material. [TS3012c: "No, wood i wood's not an option"; TS3012c: "The case, it will be the material will be rubber, suppose"]
- The approach to changeable covers changed from using them to make the product fashionable to excluding them from the basic design. [TS3012c: "one of these interchangeable covers apparently which will make it a more fashionable product"; TS3012c: "that's not something we're working with in the basic design"]

OPEN ACTIONS AND WHO OWNS THEM
- Project Manager Mark will investigate whether buttons and covers should be changed together or separately. [TS3012b: "Either either change both the buttons and and the cover or just the cover"]
- UI Designer Nick Broer will document design ideas and present them at the next meeting. [TS3012b: "I'll put some on paper and present them next time"]
- Industrial Designer Xavier Juergens will research the costs for rechargeable batteries, docking stations, LCD screens, and microphones. [TS3012b: "I'm going to try to find that out"; TS3012b: "Just to do research into both, w what it costs and what it takes for space"]
- UI Designer Nick Broer and Industrial Designer Xavier Juergens will collaborate on the final internal and external design. [TS3012c: "you should work together on the final design, both on internal and external design"]

DISAGREEMENTS STILL OPEN
- There is ongoing concern that the LCD screen and speech recognition features are too expensive to meet the 25 Euro price point. [TS3012b: "we're not going to be able to sell it for twenty-five then, with an L_C_D_ screen"; TS3012b: "Even if i if we have this lost unit, then we cannot do it for that price"]
- The team disagrees on the placement of the LCD, with objections that it is not the primary function and would force buttons into awkward positions. [TS3012b: "It's not that uh it's not the most important function, it's just an extra thing"; TS3012b: "but then you would would s have to stack away your buttons somewhere else"]
- There is debate over the feasibility of the remote locator flash, with objections that it is useless if the remote is hidden and drains battery. [TS3012b: "if it's lost in your armchair, we'll not see the flash"]
- Concerns remain that a smaller remote must be thicker to accommodate electronics, conflicting with design preferences for a slim profile. [TS3012b: "then we need to m make it a little thicker, because I have to put all the electronics in it"]
